newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan air traffic controllers end strike - media.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan air traffic controllers end strike - media.

text.p: Kenyan air traffic controllers, whose strike threatened to wreck the peak Christmas tourist season, have agreed to go back to work, local media reported on Saturday.
The controllers went on strike last weekend, demanding a 50-fold salary increase.
Kenyan state radio and the private KTN television channel said the breakthrough came after four hours of talks on Saturday between the strikers and the head of the civil service, Fares Kuindwa.
The controllers agreed to resume work on Sunday and won a pledge that their conditions of service would be reviewed, the reports said.
The Kenya Airports Authority pressed the controllers' instructors and administrators into service but the strike caused long flight delays at Nairobi and Mombasa airports.
Kenya's tourism industry had warned that foreign travel agents would cancel bookings during the busy Christmas and New Year service if the strike continued.
The controllers said their starting salary is the equivalent of only $90 a month, an assertion that was not denied by the government.
